summary: The study describes the use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to prepare zinc ferrite (ZnFe2O4) thin films for photoelectrochemical water oxidation. The ALD process involves sequential deposition of Fe2O3 and ZnO followed by thermal annealing. The films are used to investigate the photoelectrochemical performance of ZnFe2O4, showing favorable kinetics and a lower onset potential compared to hematite (Fe2O3). The study also highlights the benefits of nanostructured host–guest electrodes for enhanced light harvesting efficiency.
evidence: The text states, 'In this study, we prepare ZnFe2O4 by ALD for the first time. The resulting well-defined thin films serve as a model system, allowing an assessment of the intrinsic water photooxidation performance of zinc ferrite and comparison to ALD Fe2O3 films as an extensively studied benchmark.' Additionally, it mentions, 'Atomic layer deposition (ALD) can be used to prepare well-defined single component films as well as junction devices on smooth and structured substrates.'
